- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) in recent days, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to capture mean reversion or reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply dampening factor to peak days.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3-5 days, model often fails to adjust; prioritize downward correction if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show high volatility or extreme values, model tends to overcorrect; apply smoothing or lagged adjustment.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates later periods (e.g., 15-30d) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; reduce forecast slope for mid-to-late horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
